bib.title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection. Tsung-Yi Lin, Priya Goyal, Ross Girshick, Kaiming He, Piotr Dollár (FAIR). ICCV 2017. The PDF is arXiv:1708.02002v2, dated 7 Feb 2018.

COVERAGE: I read all 50,095 extracted chars across pages 1–10, including Appendices A–B and the references. Nothing was skipped.

CLAIMS
- claim: A one-stage detector scores about 100k locations, and the easy background ones dominate training. Two-stage detectors avoid this because proposals cut the set to 1–2k, and then sampling fixes the positive:negative ratio at 1:3.
  number: ~100k vs 1-2k, ratio 1:3, imbalance about 1:1000
  setup: dense anchor detectors in general. RetinaNet applies the loss to all of its anchors.
  quote: "enumer-ating ∼100k locations ... the training procedure is still dominated by easily classiﬁed background examples" (p2); "narrows down the number of candidate object locations to a small number (e.g., 1-2k)" (p2); "Easily classiﬁed negatives comprise the majority of the loss and dominate the gradient." (p3)
  where: p2–3

- claim: Focal loss is FL(pt) = −αt(1−pt)^γ log(pt). The defaults are γ=2 and α=0.25, and α should drop a little as γ rises.
  number: γ=2, α=.25. At pt=0.9 the loss is 100× lower than CE.
  setup: Eq. 5. It is a sigmoid per class, not softmax.
  quote: "with γ = 2, an example classiﬁed with pt = 0.9 would have 100× lower loss compared with CE and with pt≈ 0.968 it would have 1000× lower loss" (p3); "for γ = 2, α = 0.25 works best" (p5)
  where: p3, p5

- claim: Sweeping γ moves AP from 31.1 (CE) to 34.0 (γ=2). AP falls again at γ=5, and α-balanced CE peaks at α=.75.
  number: γ 0/0.1/0.2/0.5/1/2/5 gives AP 31.1/31.4/31.9/32.9/33.7/34.0/32.2. The gain is +2.9 AP.
  setup: Table 1b. ResNet-50-FPN, 600px, COCO trainval35k for training, minival for testing, best α picked for each γ.
  quote: "With γ = 2 , FL yields a 2.9 AP improvement over the α-balanced CE loss." (p7); "Setting α = .75 gives a gain of 0.9 points AP." (p7)
  where: p6 Table 1, p7

- claim: Plain CE with default initialization diverges. Setting the final classifier bias to b = −log((1−π)/π) with π=.01 makes training stable, because the many background anchors no longer produce a huge loss in the first iteration. The authors say this changes the initialization, not the loss.
  number: π=.01. CE with this init reaches 30.2 AP.
  setup: ResNet-50 RetinaNet on COCO. The authors say the result is insensitive to the exact π.
  quote: "This fails quickly, with the network diverging during training. However, simply initializing the last layer ... π = .01 ... enables effective learning ... yields a re-spectable AP of 30.2 on COCO." (p6); "this initialization prevents the large num-ber of background anchors from generating a large, desta-bilizing loss value in the ﬁrst iteration" (p6)
  where: p4 §3.3, p6

- claim: Focal loss beats the best OHEM setup by 3.2 AP.
  number: 36.0 vs 32.8 AP
  setup: Table 1d. ResNet-101-FPN, 600px, minival. The best OHEM run used batch 128, NMS .5, and no 1:3 ratio.
  quote: "achieves 32.8 AP. This is a gap of 3.2 AP, showing FL is more effective than OHEM" (p7)
  where: p7

- claim: RetinaNet reaches 39.1 AP on COCO test-dev. That is 5.9 above DSSD and 2.3 above the best two-stage model (TDM). At 600px it matches FPN Faster R-CNN while running faster.
  number: 39.1 (ResNet-101), 40.8 (ResNeXt-101). 122 ms vs 172 ms at matched accuracy. 5 fps.
  setup: RetinaNet-101-800 trained with scale jitter for 1.5× longer, which adds 1.3 AP. Timings are on an Nvidia M40 GPU. Table 1e also lists RetinaNet-50-500 at 32.5 AP/72 ms and 101-800 at 37.8 AP/198 ms.
  quote: "a healthy 5.9 point AP gap (39.1 vs. 33.2) with the closest competitor, DSSD" (p8); "matches the accuracy of the recently published ResNet-101-FPN Faster R-CNN [20], while running in 122 ms per image compared to 172 ms (both measured on an Nvidia M40 GPU)" (p8)
  where: p8, Table 2

The paper also gives these setup details, which matter for the note's anchors and NMS material:
- 9 anchors per level, from 3 scales × 3 aspect ratios. Positive if IoU ≥ 0.5, background if IoU < 0.4, ignored in between.
- Inference keeps the top 1k predictions per level above confidence 0.05, then applies NMS at 0.5.
- One square anchor alone gives 30.3 AP, and 3×3 anchors give 34.0. Gains stop beyond 6–9 anchors.
- Quote: "increasing beyond 6-9 anchors did not shown further gains" (p8).

LIMITS:
- Every result is from COCO box detection only. There is no other dataset and no segmentation.
- The paper does not cover the high-frame-rate regime: "Addressing the high frame rate regime will likely require special network design ... beyond the scope" (p8).
- The low-accuracy regime (AP<25, YOLOv2) is left out of the "upper envelope" claim.
- The paper studies only the binary loss. It calls the multi-class case "straightforward" but shows no results for it.
- Timings come from a single M40 GPU. The headline 39.1 uses longer training and scale jitter, which is not the ablation setup.
- The authors concede they tried more OHEM variants without improvement. They also say the hinge loss was unstable and gave no meaningful results.
- They concede the result has dated: "after publication, faster and more accurate results can now be obtained by a variant of Faster R-CNN from [12]" (p8).

BUILDS ON:
- R-CNN (Girshick et al., CVPR 2014) and Faster R-CNN with RPN anchors (Ren et al., NIPS 2015).
- FPN (Lin et al., CVPR 2017) as the backbone, on ResNet (He et al., CVPR 2016).
- SSD (Liu et al., ECCV 2016) and YOLO/YOLO9000 (Redmon et al., CVPR 2016/2017) as the one-stage baselines.
- OHEM (Shrivastava et al., CVPR 2016) as the comparison method.
- Bootstrapping and hard-negative mining (Sung & Poggio 1994; Viola & Jones, CVPR 2001).

CODE: none. The paper points to https://github.com/facebookresearch/Detectron (p1).

FIGURES:
- Main candidate: Fig. 1 (p1), "...adds a factor (1− pt)γ to the standard cross entropy criterion. Setting γ>0 reduces the relative loss for well-classiﬁed examples (pt>.5)". One curve plot shows γ = 0 to 5 and how easy examples get flattened, faster than reading the formula.
- Alternative: Fig. 2 (p1), a speed (ms) vs COCO AP chart comparing one-stage and two-stage detectors.
- Fig. 4 (p7), the loss CDF for negatives, shows easy negatives being discounted.

PROBLEMS:
- Superscripts were lost in extraction. "104-105 candidate locations" (p3) means 10^4–10^5. Anchor areas "322 to 5122" (p4) mean 32² to 512². "∼107 negative" (p7) means ~10^7.
- The γ symbol is missing from the figure legends.
- The PDF contained no embedded instructions.
